markdown.markdown:
Imbalance-Aware Artificial Intelligence, Urban Data Science and Reproducible Analytical Systems
![](images/profile4.png){width="170" style="border-radius:5%;float:left; margin-right:25px;margin-bottom:15px;"} ## 🔬 Research Identity ::: intro-block **Imbalance-Aware Artificial Intelligence · Urban Data Science · Reproducible Analytical Systems** Jesús Cáceres-Tello is a PhD in Statistical Studies specialising in methodological artificial intelligence and urban data science. He combines academic research with extensive experience in public sector digital systems and applied data science. His work focuses on the evaluation of predictive models under real-world constraints, with emphasis on: - Urban environmental modelling and air quality forecasting - Machine learning under class imbalance - Time series forecasting and temporal validation - Hybrid and deep learning architectures - Performance–cost trade-off analysis - Reproducible research and open science frameworks - AI-supported STEM education His research contributes to the development of transparent, reproducible, and operational AI systems for sustainable urban environments. ::: ## 🎯 Research Mission ::: intro-block The objective of his research is to develop methodologically coherent AI frameworks for urban sustainability and STEM education. This includes: - Evaluating models under structural imbalance - Designing reproducible analytical pipelines - Integrating computational efficiency into model comparison - Supporting data-driven decision-making in institutional contexts His research is developed within a broader programme in applied data science for sustainable systems. ::: ## 🏗 Research Infrastructure & Open Science ::: intro-block All research is developed following open science and reproducibility principles. All research projects are developed within a structured computational framework: - Git-based version control - Public repositories with DOI integration (Zenodo) - Reproducible scripts and notebooks (R, Python, Quarto) - Time-based validation strategies - Transparent and standardised performance reporting Each publication is supported by: - An open repository - Executable code - Structured documentation - Publicly accessible data sources This approach ensures traceability, transparency, and methodological consistency across all research outputs. ::: ## 📚 Publications & Open Repositories All publications are accompanied by open repositories, executable code, and reproducible workflows. ### 🧩 Experimental Fragility in AI-Based Predictive Systems ```{=html}

Reproducible framework for evaluating Experimental Fragility, temporal validation and distribution shift in AI-based predictive systems.

🌐 Project 📄 Article 💻 Notebook 🧪 Scripts 💾 Repository
``` ### 📊 Urban PM2.5 Methodology ```{=html}

Reproducible methodological pipeline for urban PM2.5 time series analysis (Manuscript under review. Springer Nature)

🌐 Project 📄 Article 💻 Notebook 🧪 Scripts 💾 Repository
``` ### ⚖️ Urban PM2.5 Imbalance Evaluation Framework ```{=html}

Imbalance-aware classification and performance–cost trade-off analysis (Manuscript under review. Delta, 2026)

🌐 Project 📄 Article 🧪 Scripts 💾 Repository
``` ### 📈 Urban PM2.5 Forecasting Framework ```{=html}

Reproducible forecasting framework for urban PM2.5 time series using hybrid AI models (AppliedMaths, 2024)

🌐 Project 📄 Article 💻 Notebook 🧪 Scripts 💾 Repository
``` ### 🌱 Behavioural and Institutional Drivers of Green Technology Adoption ```{=html}

TAM-based framework for sustainability transitions (Frontiers in Psychology, 2026)

🌐 Project 📄 Article 🧪 Scripts 💾 Repository
``` ### 🎓 Citizen Science and STEM Education with R ```{=html}

Reproducible AI–IoT forecasting and learning from open urban air and meteorological data (Applied Sciences, 2025)

🌐 Project 📄 Article 💻 Notebook 💾 Repository
``` ### 🧠 Quantum Computing in Data Science and STEM Education ```{=html}

Bibliometric mapping and pedagogical analysis of quantum computing tools (Computers, 2025)

🌐 Project 📄 Article 🧪 Scripts 💾 Repository
``` ## 🎓 Academic Background & Professional Experience ::: intro-block Jesús Cáceres-Tello holds: ```{=html}
  • Ph.D. candidate in Data Science (Statistical Studies), Complutense University of Madrid (expected defence: April 2026)
  • Master’s Degree in Artificial Intelligence, IoT and Big Data for Digital Transformation, INESEM Business School (2024)
  • Master’s Degree in Educational Informatics, University of Alcalá
  • B.Sc. in Information Systems Engineering, Catholic University of Ávila
  • Diploma in Computer Science (Business Informatics), University of Málaga

His professional experience includes:

  • Applied data science and artificial intelligence in public-sector environments (Madrid City Council)
  • Participation in European and national research projects in health informatics and interoperability
  • Development of data-driven systems, predictive models, and business intelligence solutions
  • Leadership and coordination of digital infrastructure and analytics initiatives
``` He has been teaching in higher education for over a decade and actively contributes to academic innovation initiatives. ::: ## 🧑‍🎓 Research Profiles ::: intro-block You can explore my professional and academic presence across several open-science platforms. These profiles provide access to publications, collaborations, datasets, and teaching activities related to environmental informatics, STEM education, and open data research. Connect with me on: ```{=html}
``` ::: ## 🤝 Collaboration ::: intro-block I welcome collaboration in: ```{=html}
  • Urban sustainability analytics
  • Methodological AI evaluation
  • Reproducible research frameworks
  • Hybrid predictive systems
  • AI-enhanced STEM education
Current research is developed within a compendium-based doctoral thesis integrating urban sustainability, methodological AI, and open science frameworks.
```
:::
